releases.body:
212NYC 2026 Gala Awards Spotlight "Humanity in Action: Staying Human in the Age of AI" 

NEW YORK, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nearly 300 of the advertising industry's most influential leaders, innovators, and changemakers gathered at Tribeca Rooftop on November 5 for 212NYC's 12th Annual Gala & Excellence Awards.

212NYC, New York's Digital Advertising Club, hosted the evening under the theme "Humanity in Action: Staying Human in the Age of AI," reflecting a pivotal moment for the industry as leaders navigate the opportunities and challenges of artificial intelligence while keeping human creativity, connection, and impact at the center. Each year, the 212NYC Gala brings together the brightest talent and most influential voices in advertising to celebrate the trailblazers, visionaries, and innovators driving the industry forward and making a lasting impact.

"The 212NYC Gala gives us an opportunity to celebrate the people moving our industry forward," said Jay Wolff, President of 212NYC. "As AI transforms how we work, connect, and create, this year's theme is a powerful reminder that our greatest asset remains our humanity. The leaders we're honoring exemplify the vision, innovation, and human impact that will define the next chapter of advertising."

The 212NYC Annual Gala is a signature gathering for the New York advertising community, bringing together leaders across media, marketing, and advertising to celebrate achievement, strengthen connections, and explore the forces shaping the industry's future.

"Since 2002, 212NYC has grown alongside the digital advertising industry, bringing people together to learn, exchange ideas, and build meaningful relationships," said Ritu Trivedi, Vice President of 212NYC. "Our community has always been driven by a willingness to embrace change while recognizing the value of human connection. This year's Gala celebrates that spirit and the people who are helping our industry innovate with purpose."

The 2026 Gala recognized five distinguished leaders whose work exemplifies this year's commitment to humanity, innovation, and impact.

The 2026 Honorees:

  • Chrissie Hanson, CEO, dentsu North America Media Practice & Global Brand President, Carat (Human-Centered Leadership Award)
  • Todd Kaplan, CMO North America, The Kraft Heinz Company (Industry Luminary Award)
  • Jeff Lucas, Chief Revenue Officer, Tubi (Breakthrough Leader Award)
  • Kory Marchisotto, President, e.l.f. Brands (Human Impact Award)
  • Nick Tran, President & CMO, First Round Collective (Innovation with Impact Award)

The evening featured keynote remarks and hosting by Rishad Tobaccowala, 212NYC's 2025 Industry Luminary Award honoree. A respected industry thinker and leader, Tobaccowala returned to this year's event to share his perspective on the evolving advertising landscape and the importance of keeping people at the heart of progress.

"We are living through a period of extraordinary technological change, but technology alone cannot determine the future we create," said Rishad Tobaccowala, keynote speaker and host of the 2026 212NYC Gala. "The real opportunity is to use AI to amplify human imagination, judgment, and connection, not replace them. I'm delighted to return to the 212NYC Gala, where this year's theme invites our industry to think deeply about what it means to innovate while staying human."

The evening was made possible through the generous support of its sponsors, including Acast, Amazon Ads, Channel Factory x Omnicom Media, CÎROC Vodka, dentsu, DoubleVerify, e.l.f. Beauty, Fanatics Advertising, Fetch, Fox, Google, iHeartMedia, Instacart Ads, Integral Ad Science, Kraft Heinz, LoopMe, Media.net, The New York Times, Peer39, Raptive, Roku, Skydance Advertising, Tubi, Vevo, Walmart Connect, WPP Media, and Zynga Ads.

 About 212NYC, New York's Digital Advertising Club

212NYC is New York's leading organization for the digital advertising industry, reaching more than 5,000 professionals across media, marketing, and advertising. 212NYC connects and educates community members through a year-round slate of compelling panels with industry leaders, signature events, and programs that advance learning and drive impact. A nonprofit, volunteer-run organization, 212NYC welcomes advertising professionals throughout the New York area. Learn more at www.212NYC.org.

New platform helps marketers challenge audience assumptions, uncover growth opportunities, and translate insights into strategic media recommendations

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Causal, an award-winning provider of advanced digital advertising solutions, today announced the launch of Causal ONE, an intelligence platform designed to transform how marketers approach audience discovery and media planning.

Causal ONE brings brand intelligence, audience discovery, media strategy, and creative inspiration together in one connected experience. Starting with a brand's website, business objectives, geographic priorities, and targeting inputs, the platform combines brand research with Causal's performance data and benchmarking capabilities to identify relevant audiences and uncover opportunities that may otherwise go unexplored.

"Causal ONE represents an important step forward for our business and how we help clients approach audience strategy," said Farshad Fardad, CEO of Causal. "We built it to challenge conventional thinking about audiences and give our teams and clients a more connected way to move from brand understanding to new opportunities. It brings together the expertise and innovation our teams have developed over the past two years in a single experience."

At the center of Causal ONE are Audience Blueprints, which provide a deeper understanding of potential audiences by explaining the signals behind them, what makes them distinct, and how they could be reached. Rather than stopping at audience identification, the platform enables users to prioritize audiences, explore channel opportunities, and connect those decisions in a strategic media plan.

Causal ONE also incorporates illustrative creative concepts, helping teams visualize potential campaign directions and make emerging strategies more tangible. By connecting audience intelligence with media recommendations and creative exploration, the platform gives marketers a more informed starting point for evaluating opportunities and developing activation strategies.

The initial experience was designed to bring greater value to the early stages of the media planning process, equipping Causal's teams with a research-led foundation for client conversations. Additional analytical capabilities extend the experience through pixel-based audience insights, live business data, and period-over-period reporting, providing further context for ongoing analysis and planning.

"As a media planner, what I love about the platform is how beautifully it brings together human expertise and agentic technology," said Shana Atwood, Vice President of Strategic Planning. "By turning our proprietary data into an intelligent starting point, we can get to recommendations faster, giving our teams more time to apply the context and nuance that technology can't replicate. Tech makes the recommendation faster and better, our people make it meaningful."

Developed through collaboration across Causal's technology, decision science, media planning, partnerships, and other teams, Causal ONE reflects the company's continued investment in connecting its capabilities into a more cohesive approach to audience intelligence and activation.

With Causal ONE, marketers can move beyond familiar audience definitions, explore new possibilities, and connect those discoveries to strategic media decisions.

releases.title: New National Study Finds Youth Sports Sponsorship Outperforms Traditional Advertising in Building Parent Trust
releases.body:
Priority Partnerships research conducted by YouGov Sport finds surprising advantages for youth sports sponsorship compared with professional sports and traditional advertising

PORTLAND, Ore., Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A new national study finds that youth sports parents are more likely to trust brands sponsoring their children's sports programs than brands advertising through traditional channels. The findings suggest an opportunity to attract more corporate investment into youth sports, potentially helping programs offset rising costs for families. 

Key findings from the Priority Partnerships Youth Sports Sponsorship Study:

  • Brand Trust: 68% say sponsorship of their child's sports program would make them likely to trust a brand, compared with 47% for TV commercials and 38% for influencer posts.
  • Brand Consideration: 71% say they would consider a brand named an Official Partner of their child's sports program, compared with 56% when the brand is an Official Partner of their favorite professional team.
  • Brand Trial: 64% say sponsorship of their child's sports program would make them likely to try a company they've never used before, compared with 51% for professional sports sponsorship and 49% for college sponsorship.

"There's a difference between seeing a company's advertisement and seeing that company support something that's important to your kids and family," said Dan Scheinman, President of Priority Partnerships. "Now we have research that shows how parents respond to that support."

As jersey sponsorships draw increased attention in professional and college sports, the research points to a potentially overlooked opportunity in youth sports. More than three-quarters (77%) of parents say they would be more likely to remember a sponsor on their child's uniform than one on the uniform of a professional sports team they follow.

The findings also have implications beyond marketing. As families and youth sports organizations contend with the rising costs of participation, corporate sponsorship represents a potential source of funding that could help support programs and reduce their reliance on registration fees.

"One of the reasons we commissioned this research is that we believe there's an opportunity to bring more corporate investment into youth sports," Scheinman said. "If brands can see the marketing value of supporting these programs, there's a stronger business case for investing in them. That has the potential to benefit the sponsors, youth sports operators, and the families these programs serve."

The complete Priority Partnerships Youth Sports Sponsorship Study is available free of charge at: www.prioritypartnerships.com/sponsorshipinyouthsportsreport.

About the Study

The study was conducted by YouGov Sport among 1,004 U.S. parents ages 25-54 with children under 18 participating in organized sports. The online survey was fielded August 27-September 3, 2026.

About Priority Partnerships

Portland, Oregon-based Priority Partnerships is a sponsorship company specializing in youth sports. Priority Partnerships represents national youth sports properties including Stronger Youth Brands, the parent company of Soccer Shots and Little Kickers, SOCCER.COM, and Girls Soccer Network. Learn more at www.prioritypartnerships.com

YouGov is a global research data and analytics group. Our mission is to offer unparalleled insight into what the world really thinks and does. With operations in the Americas, Mainland Europe, UK and Asia Pacific, we have one of the world's largest research networks. 

Above all, YouGov is powered by reality. That stems from a unique panel of millions of registered members across 64 markets, encapsulating some 18 million shopping trips and millions of interconnected data points. Our unique approach to recruiting and engaging with our panel, combined with our state-of-the-art technology platforms, enables us to deliver real-world, real-time insights that lead to better decision-making and a competitive advantage for our clients.

As innovators and pioneers of online market research, we have a strong reputation as a trusted source of accurate data and insights. Testament to this, YouGov data is regularly referenced by the global press, and we are consistently one of the most quoted market research sources in the world.

releases.title: Clear Channel Outdoor Renews and Expands Advertising Partnership with Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport
releases.body:
Competitive Renewal Launches New Era of Digital, Experiential and Branded Media as ECP Undergoes Major Terminal Expansion

PANAMA CITY, Fla., Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clear Channel Outdoor (CCO)'s Airports Division, the leading U.S. airport sponsorship and advertising partner, has renewed and expanded its longstanding partnership with Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport (ECP). Originally established in 2005 and reselected through a competitive process, the renewed agreement reflects two decades of operational performance and the airport's confidence in CCO's ability to deliver on its next chapter of growth.

The agreement comes as ECP undertakes a major terminal expansion and modernization project, creating an opportunity for CCO to invest more into the airport's advertising program with new digital media, experiential activations and refreshed displays. The centerpiece of the new program will be a network of double-sided digital flags throughout the concourse, introducing dynamic content and a contemporary digital media presence that integrates seamlessly and enhances the terminal environment.

Under the new agreement, CCO will make a significant investment in ECP's advertising infrastructure over an initial three-year contract term and with the opportunity to renew. The investment will support the evolution of a curated and contemporary advertising program, with strategically positioned state-of-the-art media that complements the passenger experience and the airport's sense of place. The program will provide greater flexibility for advertisers while creating new opportunities for brands to engage travelers and support ECP's long-term commercial growth.

"ECP is a market that performs well above its size, and this renewal is a reflection of what a strong collaborative partnership produces over time," said Morten Gotterup, president, Clear Channel Outdoor's Airports Division. "As ECP invests in the next generation of its terminal, we have an opportunity to invest into that experience and to build something that reflects both where this airport is today and where it's headed. Our new program will bring together digital, experiential and high-impact media to continue to delight passengers and the brands that want to reach them for years to come."

ECP has experienced sustained growth since opening in 2010, serving a record 1.9 million passengers in 2025 representing a 3.1% year-over-year increase. The airport serves large, leisure-oriented audiences, with travelers visiting Northwest Florida's Emerald Coast for vacations, weekend getaways and outdoor recreation. Through nonstop and seasonal service from American, Delta, Southwest and United Airlines, ECP connects the region with major markets including Atlanta, Nashville, Dallas, Denver, Houston, New York, Chicago and Baltimore. That traveler profile—arriving and ready to engage—makes ECP a compelling platform for brands looking to connect with consumers at the start of their trip.

"As ECP undergoes this major Terminal Expansion, we are focused on enhancing every element of the traveler experience. Clear Channel's commitment to investing in state-of-the-art digital infrastructure and experiential activations will not only modernize our concourses but also provide powerful new avenues for local and national brands to connect with our growing passenger base. We are proud to build upon our history together and look forward to a new era of innovation that supports ECP's long-term commercial vitality," stated ECP Executive Director Parker W. McClellan Jr., A.A.E.

The renewed partnership reflects CCO and ECP's shared commitment to evolving the airport experience alongside the continued growth of Northwest Florida. As construction progresses toward the terminal expansion's 2029 completion, the new advertising program will provide a flexible platform that grows with the airport creating new opportunities for brands to connect with travelers while supporting ECP's long-term revenue goals.

To learn more about Clear Channel Airports, visit https://clearchanneloutdoor.com/airport-advertising/.

About Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc.

Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. is at the forefront of driving innovation in the out-of-home advertising industry. Our dynamic advertising platform is broadening the pool of advertisers using its medium through the expansion of digital billboards and displays and the integration of data analytics and programmatic capabilities that deliver measurable campaigns that are simpler to buy. By leveraging the scale, reach and flexibility of our diverse portfolio of assets, we connect advertisers with millions of consumers every month.

releases.title: Cuttable Unveils Next-Generation AI Advertising Platform as U.S. Expansion Accelerates
releases.body:
The platform's evolution comes alongside an A$20 million Series A funding round led by Airtree Ventures, marking Cuttable's next phase of growth as it moves beyond AI ad generation.

NEW YORK, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cuttable, an AI-powered creative production platform for performance marketing teams, today unveiled the next evolution of its platform, designed to help brands move beyond generating ads to understand what works and make smarter decisions about what to create next. Just one year after entering the U.S. market, the Australian-founded company now generates 40% of its revenue from the region.

While AI has made producing ads faster and easier, knowing which creative to make next remains a challenge. Most tools focus on either generating ads or analyzing their performance, leaving marketers to connect the dots between what they intend to test, what actually worked and what to create next.

Cuttable brings those pieces together. Its evolved platform connects a brand's creative assets, customer data and performance history with the marketer's original intent, building on what the brand has already tried rather than starting from scratch with each new creative brief.

Cuttable's software was built to remove creative as a bottleneck for performance marketing teams producing, testing and rebuilding ads at scale. The platform reads a brand's website, social channels and guidelines to build an editable brand strategy and brand kit. From there, marketers can write a brief in plain language and receive finished, editable ads, built using existing brand and product assets or Cuttable's AI content studio, Shoots, which creates and extends photo and video content.

Most media plans still start in a spreadsheet, and every agency, team, market and client lays them out differently. Getting a plan into a system of record has meant re-entering it by hand, which takes time, introduces errors, and delays the moment when finance, leadership and operations teams can see and act on the plan. With the AI Ingestion Agent, planning teams can:

  • Start from their existing file. Upload an Excel or CSV file to create a new plan.
  • Automate field mapping. The agent reads each column and suggests how it maps to the customer's plan templates and fields.

  • Use the plan right away. Once confirmed, the plan is structured data that can be used for reporting, budget tracking and actuals reconciliation.

Uploaded files are validated so that only supported plan formats are processed, and customer plan data is not used to train AI models. Each upload is saved as a new plan version rather than overwriting earlier work, so every change can be traced. This new product capability ships with enterprise controls. It is opt-in and enabled per customer. This first release creates new plans from spreadsheets; updating existing plans and bulk-importing historical ones will follow.

releases.body:
First-to-market capability brings together Acxiom, Omni, and Rembrand's VISTA platform, with access to premium inventory from major media partners

NEW YORK, Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Omnicom Media, an Omnicom (NYSE: OMC) Connected Capability, and in-content advertising platform Rembrand are partnering to bring in-content advertising into the mainstream media mix with a first-to-market capability that enables brands to identify, plan, and activate in-content placements across first-look premium streaming inventory from multiple major media companies.

The partnership provides OM's Content Collective – the group's branded content center of excellence - first-mover access to Rembrand's AI-powered VISTA platform, which scans publisher content to identify scenes that can be monetized by insertion of in-content advertising. Using AcxiomRealID™ and direct integrations with major streamers, brands can identify the most relevant content for a given audience. Pairing this intelligence with Rembrand's VISTA platform, brands unlock a more systematic and scalable way to find relevant programming and activate against those opportunities across participating streaming partners.

Historically, in-content advertising has been managed through bespoke partnerships and individual content integrations. The new capability brings those opportunities into a common planning framework, giving media teams visibility across participating publishers and allowing in-content placements to be considered alongside broader media investments.

The collaboration is rooted in a fundamental shift in consumer behavior. Omnicom Media's recent research, From Tuned Out to Leaned In: How to Combat Ad Avoidance, found that 65% of U.S. consumers avoid advertising to some degree, whether by skipping, scrolling, muting, or ignoring ads. As consumers use subscriptions, apps, AI, and other tools to exert greater control over their media experiences, brands need new ways to reach people without creating another interruption.

Additionally, commissioned research conducted by Omnicom Media's Partner Intelligence team in collaboration with Rembrand evaluated the effectiveness of in-content advertising, finding that, when paired with traditional video ads, perceptions of premium content amplify the performance of ICAs, driving a 5.5 times impact on message recall, and a 4x increase in both purchase intent and perceptions of the brand as premium.

"Our research identified how quickly consumers actively or passively disengage when advertising feels intrusive or overly repetitive," said Megan Pagliuca, Chief Product Officer, Omnicom Media. "To address this, we have launched new capabilities in streaming to address negative reach, improve relevance and measurability of traditional brand experiences, and now we are complementing these with a first of its kind data driven, scalable approach to in-content advertising."

How It Works

The capability connects four stages:

  • Audience matching: Acxiom audience segments are matched with streaming viewership data to identify shows, movies, and genres that best index with a target audience.
  • Inventory mapping: Relevant programming is matched against in-content advertising opportunities available through VISTA.
  • Inventory expansion: Additional content can be onboarded through established processes with participating streaming partners when relevant opportunities are not yet available.
  • Activation: Brands deploy in-content placements against selected audiences and programming across participating publishers.

The result is a way to put brands directly into content consumers have chosen to watch, while providing greater visibility into in-content supply across publishers.

"In-content advertising has always offered brands the opportunity to show up within content people have actively chosen to watch," said John Sedlak, Chief Revenue Officer, Rembrand. "Our collaboration with Omnicom Media makes those opportunities easier to identify, plan and activate across premium streaming, bringing a new level of scale and consistency to the category."

Applications range from an automaker placing a new model in relevant programming across a streamer, using Acxiom in-market auto segments to reach shoppers who routinely avoid traditional ads, to a beverage brand appearing in top-indexing summer programming during key seasonal purchase periods. Retail brands can similarly use in-content placements to directly connect exposure to the path to purchase.

Summing up the response to-date from clients who have been briefed on the new capability, Jillian Davis, Director of Marketing Technology for Auto Trader and Kelly Blue Book parent company Cox Automotive said, "We're always eager to leverage new, scalable and organic ways to reach our customers within premium content."

NEW YORK and LONDON , Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- pubX, which builds agent-to-agent infrastructure for advertising, today announced a $5 million Series A led by Chicago Ventures and the acquisition of Compliant, the media quality and governance company. Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. Compliant will retain its name and operate as a pubX company, led by CEO Jamie Barnard. Within pubX, Jamie will take the role of President, Global Demand Growth, leading the company's global growth strategy across agencies, advertisers and the wider buy-side.

pubX builds the agents that plan, buy, sell and optimize advertising — and the infrastructure they transact on. Its buyer agents and seller agents work directly with one another, from brief to reporting, across every channel, so that more of every dollar reaches the media and the publisher behind it. pubX began on the publisher side, spending years helping publishers price and sell their inventory. Compliant, founded by former Unilever and P&G executives, has focused principally on the demand side, delivering measurable value to global brands and their agencies. The acquisition unites brand and publisher in one company, and that experience, on both sides of the market is what shaped the company's vision for something new: infrastructure designed from the ground up for agents to buy and sell directly. Built on the open Ad Context Protocol (AdCP), it works for buyer and seller alike.

Trust as the founding product principle

pubX was built on the premise that no one hands their media budget to a system they don't trust, so trust, transparency, and accountability are built into the infrastructure itself, on both sides of every transaction. Its agents are educated by pubX: governance checks on every buy, decisions that are reasoned, traced and auditable, with Compliant's quality signals shaping what they consider. The agents are guided by the client, on the brand's own brief, plan, publishers and commercial rules. People stay in control: the client sets the level of autonomy and approves the plan at key stages, and the agents execute inside those rules. As trust is earned, autonomy grows.

"Programmatic took this industry from fax machines and spreadsheets into more automated and real-time platforms in two short decades, and everything we've done since builds on that premise," said Andrew Mole, CEO and co-founder of pubX. "Agents let us finish what was started. You tell them how you buy, you sign off where it matters, and every page of the brief gets read every single time. For the first time, the infrastructure has caught up with what brands want to achieve with their advertising and how publishers want to sell."

"For years, brands have searched for high-quality, high-performing inventory with real, relevant and engaged audiences. Compliant built the Data Integrity and CTV Quality Indexes so that they could do that with certainty rather than speculation," said Jamie Barnard, CEO of Compliant. "Inside pubX, those media quality and governance signals sit in the decision itself, so an agent weighs them before it buys. This is what gives each CMO the confidence to trust pubX's agents."

"Every part of the advertising industry is asking how agents will improve buying and selling, and most answers so far are an agentic layer built on existing infrastructure. Co-founders Andrew Mole and Alex Rosen, pubX's CTO, have built advertising infrastructure before, and this time they built it for agents from the start, on both sides of the transaction, with a publisher base that already trusts them and a design that keeps the client in control. That is a rare starting position, and the Compliant acquisition makes it stronger," said Stuart Larkins, Co-founder & General Partner at Chicago Ventures.

The funding will support pubX's expansion in the United States, the build-out of its demand-side business serving brands and agencies, continued development of its buyer and seller agents on AdCP, and the integration of Compliant's signals across the platform.

"For a publisher, agentic buying is about discoverability. Buyer agents see the audiences and environments we actually have, backed by our first-party data, and that puts us in front of spend that never reached us before, in an environment we can win. It amplifies what our sales team already does well," said Stephanie Mazzamaro, Head of Revenue and Data, Paradium.AI, formerly The Arena Group.

"As advertising increasingly moves toward agentic buying, discoverability becomes critical," said Jason Taylor, Chief Revenue Officer, USA TODAY Co. "Publishers that invest in trusted content, engaged audiences, and brand-safe environments should be more visible to AI-powered buying platforms. The opportunity is to create a more transparent marketplace where quality is recognized and rewarded."

pubX at Advertising Week New York

On Wednesday, October 7, pubX will run a live agent-to-agent media buy at a private executive lunch during Advertising Week New York. A campaign for Reckitt's Mucinex brand will go from brief to live placement, with Reckitt's trading team approving the plan at key stages and publishers including Paradium.AI and USA TODAY Co. reviewing and accepting the campaign as it happens. Attendance is by invitation.

pubX builds agent-to-agent infrastructure for advertising. Its buyer and seller agents, educated by pubX, trained by the client, and governed on both sides of every transaction, let brands, agencies and publishers plan, buy, sell and optimize media directly, with trust earned one campaign at a time. Learn more at www.pubx.ai

Compliant, a pubX company, is the media quality and governance company behind the Data Integrity and CTV Quality Indexes, used by leading global advertisers and industry bodies to measure data integrity and media quality across the supply chain. Learn more at www.compliant.global

Chicago Ventures is a seed-stage venture capital fund founded to fill a market gap in early-stage capital for tech companies outside traditional hubs like Silicon Valley, focusing on undercapitalized tech ecosystems in the Central U.S. and beyond. They lead seed rounds "before it's obvious" and operate a formal platform function that serves as a direct extension of portfolio companies' teams, with their network explicitly architected to provide customer introductions, expert help, and talent access at scale rather than just for sourcing deals. Learn more at www.chicagoventures.com

Sports investment extends far beyond the traditional media buy. Brands advertise across TV broadcast and exclusive live streaming sports while simultaneously investing in teams, leagues, athletes and major sporting events through broadcast integrations, virtual placements, in-venue signage, equipment sponsorships and creative campaigns.

"What's especially exciting in sports right now is the innovation happening around how brands can participate," said Jay Nielsen, VP of Product at MediaRadar. "New formats, integrations and sponsorship opportunities are creating more ways for advertisers to show up. Total Event Investment brings those signals together to reveal the broader strategy behind how brands are investing across sports."

Beyond the Media Buy

Total Event Investment grew from MediaRadar's research surrounding the 2026 Men's World Cup, where 6,737 brands invested $1.42 billion across advertising, official sponsorships, athlete and national team partnerships and creative campaigns.

That work helped shape MediaRadar's expansion into sponsorship analytics, complementing its existing TV broadcast and exclusive live streaming sports advertising coverage.

MediaRadar customers can now explore sponsorship signals alongside MediaRadar's Creative, Competitive, Commercial and Market Intelligence to understand how advertising, sponsorship and creative work together as part of a broader brand strategy.

Computer Vision Expands Sponsorship Intelligence

MediaRadar's proprietary Logo Recognition technology uses computer vision to identify brand logos and on-screen placements, transforming visual brand exposure into structured sponsorship intelligence.

Logo Recognition builds on MediaRadar's proprietary Classification Engine, which uses machine learning to organize and enrich advertising data at scale. Together, these capabilities expand the signals MediaRadar can identify, structure and connect through Total Event Investment.

From Media Occurrence to Brand Commitment

While developed through a sports lens, Total Event Investment can extend to other cultural moments, from a championship game or awards show to a month-long tournament or season.

The framework examines how brands show up before, during and after that moment across media investment, sponsorship, creative strategy, activation timing and cross-channel presence, moving beyond individual media occurrences to understand the broader brand commitment surrounding an event.

Understanding the Full Partnership

"When MediaRadar first released Live Streaming Sports in 2025, adding the coverage to our intelligence stack was a no-brainer," said Brett Joss, Head of Sponsorship Sales at Jomboy Media. "While baseball is core to our business, we need visibility into brands investing across other marquee sports. For brands and agencies, Sports Intelligence provides a way to benchmark competitors, understand multi-sport investment strategies and see how sponsorship connects to paid advertising and creative. The conversation continues October 22 during MediaRadar's State of the Industry webinar, State of the Industry: The Convergence of Sports, Culture & Creative, exploring how advertising, sponsorship and creative converge around the moments that capture audience attention.

NEW YORK, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GrowthLoop, a pioneer in agentic AI-powered marketing solutions, today released its 2026 Commerce Media Investment Index, revealing that activation speed and audience options have become decisive factors in where advertisers place retail and commerce media budgets. Conducted in partnership with Ascend2, the study surveyed nearly 300 U.S. and Canadian marketing professionals involved in retail media network (RMN) or commerce media network (CMN) advertising decisions.

The findings reveal what motivates advertisers to spend more with network partners and shed light on how execution friction could put that spend at risk:

  • 86% say slow audience fulfillment could cause them to reduce spend or leave a network partner, while 85% say they would pay a premium for same-day fulfillment.  
  • Nearly all respondents indicate that access to more segments would make them more likely to increase spend.
  • 32% of advertisers have reduced, paused, or reconsidered investment because of difficulty proving ROI to leadership.

"Advertisers are telling media networks how to win more budget: Provide better audiences, activate them faster, and deliver meaningful results quickly enough to inform the next campaign," said Anthony Rotio, co-founder and co-CEO of GrowthLoop. "As we've seen with customers like Gopuff, a warehouse-native audience building solution is the way to fulfill these requirements and ultimately build stronger advertiser relationships."

Key report findings

The Index shows that advertisers spread significant budget across a crowded commerce media market. The majority of advertisers allocate at least 15% of their digital advertising budgets to these networks and 90% work with two or more RMN or CMN partners. No respondents plan to decrease commerce media spend in the next year, and a full 85% plan to increase their spend.

Additional findings include:

Speed shapes spending decisions

  • 92% would be more likely to increase spend with faster audience fulfillment.
  • 94% would likely spend more with partners offering self-service audience-building tools.
  • Advertisers reporting the strongest ROI are five times more likely than others to receive custom audiences the same day.

Advertisers want more audience choice

  • Only 38% are extremely satisfied with the number of audiences available through their partners.
  • 95% say they would be more likely to increase spend with access to more segments.

Confidence in incrementality measurement drives investment and ROI

  • Only 40% are very confident in their partners' incrementality measurement.
  • Advertisers with high confidence in their partners' measurement spend a larger share of their digital budget on RMN/CMN and are more than twice as likely to significantly exceed ROI targets.

Campaign results often arrive too late to guide the next decision

  • Nearly half of advertisers wait at least one week for post-campaign performance data, while only 8% receive it the same day.
  • Just 32% say they can consistently use campaign results to optimize future audience targeting.

As audience speed and scale remain top of mind for advertisers, Gopuff — the leading instant commerce platform that delivers thousands of everyday products to customers in minutes — has shown how media networks can successfully address these priorities. "After implementing a warehouse-native stack, we increased our audience segments from 100 to more than 600, and expanded audiences for our subsidiary, BevMo!, from 75 to 400. These expanded audience catalogs give our internal teams and brand partners a broader range of ready-to-use targeting options and create the groundwork for more customized segment offerings."
